title: Reorganize String
prompt: Given a string `s`, rearrange the characters of `s` so that no two adjacent characters are the same. Return any valid rearrangement, or an empty string `""` if no valid rearrangement exists.

examples.explanation: "aba" has no two adjacent characters equal, and uses the same letters as "aab".
There is no way to rearrange "aaab" so that no two 'a's are adjacent, since 'a' appears 3 times among only 4 characters.
A single character has no adjacent pair to worry about, so it's trivially already a valid arrangement.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: If any character's frequency exceeds ceil(length / 2), no valid arrangement can exist — check this early as a feasibility condition.
Greedily placing the currently most frequent remaining character next tends to spread out high-frequency letters, avoiding forced adjacency.

Use a max-heap of (count, character); pop the most frequent character to place, then hold it back for one round (don't push it back immediately) so it can't be placed immediately adjacent to itself again.

solution.approach: Count character frequencies and push them onto a max-heap (negated counts for Python's heapq). Repeatedly pop the most frequent character and append it to the result, but withhold it from re-entering the heap until after the next character has been placed — this guarantees it never sits directly next to another copy of itself. If the heap empties while a withheld character still has remaining count greater than zero and there's nothing else to place beside it, no valid arrangement exists. This greedy strategy works because always using the currently-most-frequent character maximally delays when that character must repeat.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n log k) where n is the length of s and k is the number of distinct characters
